answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may vote on shared work, then slash that bond when a randomly audited task reveals fabricated results. Audits sample claims rather than trusting reputation, so splitting one operator into many accounts does not multiply influence: each account needs capital at risk, and colluding accounts can lose it together. A lotus report, a yarrow review, and a glacier benchmark can all enter the same audit queue. The attacker pays for every identity and risks forfeiting its stake.
